newsitem.title: THAILAND: Australian envoy helps foreigners flee Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Australian envoy helps foreigners flee Cambodia.

text.p: A group of 41 expatriates led by the Australian Defence Attache fled fighting in Cambodia and crossed the border into eastern Thailand on Monday evening, the attache and immigration officials said.
It was the second group of expatriates brought out by Colonel David Mead from Battambang in northwestern Cambodia. On Sunday he crossed the border in a 60-strong group.
The group arrived at Poipet on the border with this Thai town in 11 trucks.
Mead told reporters the expatriates were mostly non-governmental organisation workers and UNICEF officials working in western Cambodia.
They included 10 Americans, nine French, nine Japanese, four Canadians and three Britons. There were others of various nationalities, including some Thais, officials said.

A Thai man evacuated from Battambang told reporters the situation was becoming more tense. He said they saw three military trucks loaded with soldiers at checkpoints about 10 km (six miles) from Battambang but did not know which faction the soldiers belonged to.
Fighting has been heating up in northwestern Cambodia between troops loyal to the country's rival prime ministers.
Strongman Hun Sen took control of the capital Phnom Penh on Monday and said First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh -- who is in France -- no longer had his job.
Ranariddh accused Hun Sen of staging a coup and said in an interview published in Paris he was mounting a resistance.
Phnom Penh's airport has been closed since Saturday due to the fighting.
